chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Abu Baseer who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a group of people who accompanied each other on a journey as friends, so one of them stole the belongings of the other. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'This is treachery; he would not be cut (for haram theft), but he would be pursued for his theft and his treachery.'

It was said to him (peace be upon him), 'So if one steals from the house of his own father?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'He would not be cut, because a son of the man is not barred from entering the house of his father. This is treachery, and similar to that is the one who steals from the house of his brother, and his sister, when he enters (their house), as he is not barred from the entering.'

key_terms.يُقْطَعُ: To be cut (referring to the fixed punishment for theft)

ai.seo_question: Does stealing from one's father or brother incur the fixed punishment of cutting in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Baqir (AS), the distinction is drawn between the fixed corporal punishment (hadd) for theft and the civil liability for restitution, emphasizing that close kinship or shared residence negates the 'barrier to entry' (hijab) required for the hadd to apply. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that familial intimacy precludes the severity of amputation, shifting the focus to compensating for the loss and acknowledging the moral breach of trust (khiyanah). It serves as a key precedent in al-Kafi for understanding how social proximity modifies legal penalties in Islamic law.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Abu Baseer who said,

‘I asked Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> about a group of people who accompany each other on a journey of friends, so one of them steals the belongings of the other. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘This is treachery, he would not be cut, but he would be followed due to his theft and his treachery’.

It was said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘So if one steals from the house of his own father?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He would not be cut, because a son of the man is not barred from entering the house of his father. This is treachery, and similar to that is the one who steals from the house of his brother, and his sister, when he enters (their house), as he is not barred from the entering’.
